question: Question linked to the image nº9 11-year-old boy who attends because 10 days ago he has a daily fever of predominance in the evening. In the last 2 days the fever has been increasing (up to 38.5º C). Has little appetite and has lost weight (2 kg). Three weeks ago he was kicked in the right knee. Although initially he only had pain later he noticed inflammation, which was increasing until it prevented him from walking. Analytical: elevation of PCR (75 mg / L) without other significant alterations. Simple radiology is shown. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
analysis: The clinical presentation of an 11-year-old boy with a history of trauma to the knee, persistent fever, weight loss, and elevated C-reactive protein (CRP) suggests an inflammatory or infectious process. The key details include the recent trauma, progressive knee inflammation, and systemic symptoms like fever and weight loss. Osteomyelitis, an infection of the bone, often presents with fever, localized pain, and elevated inflammatory markers, especially following trauma. The other options, such as ossifying myositis, eosinophilic granuloma, osteosarcoma, and osteoblastoma, are less consistent with the acute systemic symptoms and the history of trauma. Osteosarcoma could present with pain and swelling, but the acute fever and systemic symptoms are more indicative of an infectious process like osteomyelitis.
